text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated 5xx rate detected for model-runtime in us-west-2. Error spike from 02:09 -> 02:16 UTC. Symptoms: segfaults and OOM logs from runner group 'mr-serve-3'. Auto-mitigation attempted: routed 25% traffic to fallback-model-v1.2. See /incidents/heap-tracker for details.

alex: I'm on call, ack. Looking at Grafana — error rate from ~0.5% -> 12% on /v1/generate and /v1/stream. Latency also spiking. Rolling error distribution: mostly long-context requests (>16k tokens) hitting same hosts.

maya: @alex can you paste a sample of the runner logs? I want the segfault stack sample and dmesg. Could be a runaway kernel allocation after quantized kernel hotpath.

alex: here's tail from one of the failing pods (mr-serve-3-7f9):

```
[2026-03-15T02:10:12Z] runtime error: signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code 1, fault addr 0x7f3b9c000
model_runner: segfault at kv_cache_write+0x4a
Stack backtrace:
  0x7f3b9c000 kv_cache_write
  0x7f3b8fabc model_step
  0x7f3b8e000 request_handler
  0x7f3b7f000 main_loop
```

and dmesg snippet:

```
Mar 15 02:10:11 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 22345 (model_runner) total-vm: 6xxxxkB, anon-rss: 5xxxxkB
Mar 15 02:10:11 kernel: oom_reaper: reaped process 22345
```

maya: thanks. That looks like a combined segfault+OOM. Could be memory pressure leading to corrupt state on next allocation. Are we seeing any page faults / thrashing? Can we get `smem` or `pmap`?

ryan: jumping in — we pushed a model change yesterday that added a new continuous-kv caching path for long contexts. My guess: an uninitialized pointer in the new cache resize logic. I can look for reproducer but need a safe mitigation.

jordan_ops: mitigation steps proposal:
  1) Temporarily reduce max_context_tokens for hosted routes from 64k -> 8k (config flag) to prevent long-context requests from hitting the new path.
  2) Scale mr-serve-3 node pool up by +30% to give headroom while we investigate.
  3) Drain and restart pods that are reporting segfaults to clear corrupt state.
  4) Keep fallback-model traffic at 50% if error rate doesn't improve in 5m.

alex: executing step 1 now: updating route config for customer-facing routes. Pushing config change.

deploy-bot: config-change: route-limits updated by alex. Context cap reduced to 8k for routes: /v1/generate, /v1/stream. Deployment id: dpl-55432

alex: step 1 applied. Monitoring...

maya: while that rolls, collect a full core dump from a failing pod before restart. Use `gcore` and upload to s3://redwood-incident-cores/1765554321/. We need to confirm whether kernel OOM triggered before segfault or vice versa.

ryan: I can roll a hotfix branch to disable the new continuous-kv path (`CONT_KV=false`) in runtime build and publish a canary image. But that will take ~15-20m to build and smoke test.

sam_cs: heads-up — we're seeing inbound tickets from two customers experiencing 502/504. I'm triaging severity; Lina, customers asking for ETA.

lina_pm: @sam_cs flagging enterprise customers on dedicated nodes — are they impacted or just hosted? We need clear customer impact statement forstatus.redwood.ai.

jordan_ops: quick check: dedicated clusters show normal error rates. Impact appears concentrated on hosted pool mr-serve-3 in us-west-2. CS: prepare a brief message: "Experiencing increased 5xx from text generation routes in US-WEST. We're rolling mitigations and limiting long-context requests. Expect reduced availability for long-context jobs. Further updates in 30m."

sam_cs: drafting now.

alex: after config change error rate dropped to ~3% from 12% but still elevated. Some pods still segfaulting during heavy requests. Proceeding to drain and restart 3 pods now.

deploy-bot: pod-restart: mr-serve-3-7f9 restarted by alex. pod mr-serve-3-5c2 draining.

maya: pulling core from s3. Initial quickbacktrace shows invalid free inside `kv_resize`. Candidate repro: repeated allocate+free under heavy concurrent append.

ryan: starting hotfix build now that we have a likely safe revert. I'll open PR to gate the continuous-kv path behind a runtime flag and publish image rc-1765-hotfix.

alex: scaling nodepool +30% (adding 4 nodes). ETA ~4m.

jordan_ops: scaling started. Also enabling extra eviction policy to favor large-context requests being rejected earlier (429) instead of saturating memory.

sam_cs: posted status update to customers: "We've limited max context length while we investigate. Short context requests unaffected. We're prioritizing recovery and will update within 30m." Links: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1765554321

maya: one more datapoint: tracing shows many concurrent requests that include large function calls (tooling) causing multiple KV writes per token. That increases memory churn.

ryan: hotfix image built and pushed to canary pool. Rolling canary to 3 nodes with `CONT_KV=false`.

deploy-bot: rollout: image rc-1765-hotfix deployed to canary subset (3 pods). Health checks passing.

alex: canary looks good, error rate on those pods ~0.1%. Promoting to wider rollout; will do safe 20%->50% if stable for 3m.

maya: keep collecting cores from older pods for postmortem. Save logs, note kernel OOM timing. We'll likely add stronger allocation checks and a debug guard in kv_resize.

lina_pm: CS reported initial customer impact: 12 enterprise requests experiencing 502s, 78 developer orgs saw increased latency. No data exfiltration. Logging and audit unaffected. We'll publish summary after incident.

sam_cs: updating enterprise customers directly with ETA: "Mitigation in progress; expected recovery within 30 minutes. We will follow up with root cause and remediation plan."

alex: after wider rollout and context cap, overall error dropped to 0.6% and latency normalized. I'm going to mark this as mitigated but keeping on-call to monitor for 1h.

incident-bot: Incident severity: degraded -> mitigated. Auto-close timer set to 60m. Please file postmortem with timeline, root cause (probable uninit pointer in continuous-kv), and customer impact (CS notes). Tag: mr-kv-176555.

ryan: filing PR with unit/integration test to reproduce concurrent kv_resize and adding ASAN/UBSAN in the hotpath. Will attach core diffs.

maya: leaving runbook note: when paging/large-context errors spike, first step reduce context cap for hosted routes and route to fallback model; collect cores before restarts; enable eviction policy to reject large contexts early.

lina_pm: thanks team. Sam, prepare a short external postmortem (customer-friendly) once we have the RCA. I'll coordinate internal detailed postmortem with eng+sre.

sam_cs: noted. Will draft and share in #status-review.

alex: handing off to maya for monitoring and postmortem. I'm out for now. :thumbsup:

maya: taking on-call handoff. Will keep an eye on related alerts and start timeline doc. Closing thread in 10m if stable.

— end of thread —
